newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore plans social work for youth delinquents.
newsitem.headline: Singapore plans social work for youth delinquents.

text.p: Singapore intends to put troubled teenagers into tough social work programmes to help curb rising juvenile delinquency.

A Ministry of Community Development (MCD) spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday that starting this month teenage offenders must complete some 40 hours of community work in homes for the aged or child-care centres while on probation.

Singapore is known for enforcing strict codes of social conduct, and the pilot project to implement Community Service Orders (CSOs) is one of many aimed at what is perceived as a growing social problem in the city-state.

"The rehabilitation of juvenile offenders is an ongoing philosophy of the government, that the offenders should, as much as possible, be rehabilitated within the community and with the support of their families," the MCD spokesman said.
"MCD works together with the police and courts in dealing with the problem of juvenile delinquency," he said.

The project would be conducted over an eight-month period during which selected youths not involved in violent offences would be required to cook, clean and collect donations for homes and community centers.
They will learn social skills through mingling with other children and the elderly, the MCD said.

CSOs for offenders between 14 and 16 years old are among other measures recommended by the Inter-Ministry Committee on Dysfunctional Families, Juvenile Delinquency and Drug Abuse to tackle rising juvenile crime.
In the first 10 months of this year, 1,753 youths were arrested for juvenile offenses, compared with 2,187 arrests made over the same period in 1995.
But the recent drop in arrest numbers belies an overall rise in juvenile crime since 1990. Juvenile arrests have doubled from 1,205 arrests in 1990 to 2,589 in for all of 1995.
